mainTopic: Young children and the laws of נדה and זיבה, which discharges make a man or a woman impure, and the bedding of a בועל נדה compared to a זב.
overview: The גמרא explains that the extra word "ואשה" in the נדה verse teaches that a man is not impure through a red discharge. It shows that a ten-day-old girl's זיבה needs its own verse, and that this verse already tells us a baby girl can be a נדה, since there is no זבה without נדה. That leaves the נדה verse free to exclude a man from red; a second exclusion covers blood as well as red semen. Next, a ברייתא teaches that even a one-day-old boy can be a זב, either from "איש איש" (רבי יהודה) or from "לזכר ולנקבה" (רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה). Another ברייתא includes a boy in the laws of semen only from nine years and one day. רבא settles the clash: the nine-year rule is a tradition from סיני, the baby rule comes from the פסוק, and the extra word teaches that a white discharge does not make a woman a זבה. A צריכותא explains why the baby rule is written for both boys and girls. Finally, the גמרא explains the משנה about כותים: bedding under a בועל נדה is like bedding above a זב, making only food and drink impure. It then starts to find the source in the פסוק "תחתיו", and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The extra verse comes to exclude a man from red discharge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers an earlier question: the extra word in the נדה verse comes to teach that a man does not become impure through a red discharge.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse comes to exclude a man from becoming impure through red.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers a question asked just before this point: why do we need the extra word "ואשה" in the נדה verse? Its answer is that the word teaches that a man is not made impure by red.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman becomes טמאה through blood, which is red. The extra word "woman" limits this: only a woman becomes impure through red, and a man does not.

keyTerms.meaning: To exclude; to teach that something is left out
A woman impure because of her monthly period

phrases.english: To exclude a man from red.
phrases.notes: He means a man does not become impure from a red discharge; that kind of טומאה is only for a woman.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question raised just before this section about why the extra word in the נדה verse is needed.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives the extra word a new purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The extra word "ואשה" seemed to have no job.
steps.terutzMaskana: It teaches that a man is not impure through red.

steps.title: A ברייתא uses "ואשה" for a ten-day-old זבה. Why not learn it from נדה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that learns from "ואשה" that a ten-day-old girl can be a זבה, and asks why a verse is needed when this could be learned from נדה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about what was taught: "Woman" teaches me only about an adult woman. From where do I know that a ten-day-old girl can become a זבה? The verse says "And a woman." Why do I need this? Let us learn it from נדה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that uses the extra "ו" of "ואשה" to include a ten-day-old girl in the laws of זיבה. It asks why a verse is needed for this, since we already know that even a baby girl can be a נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a one-day-old girl can be a נדה, it seems obvious that a ten-day-old can be a זבה, so the verse looks extra. This challenge sets up the larger question of which verse is truly needed and which is free for other teachings.

keyTerms.meaning: Impurity from bleeding outside the normal time of the period
Let us learn it (from another case)

phrases.english: But what about that which was taught:
"Woman": I have only a woman,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 15:25. "Woman" sounds like a grown woman.

phrases.english: from where do we know that a ten-day-old girl is subject to זיבה?
The verse says, "And a woman."
Why do I need this? Let us learn it from נדה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises a related verse whose need seems questionable.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's use of "ואשה" to include a ten-day-old girl in זיבה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since a one-day-old girl is already a נדה, a ten-day-old girl's זיבה should follow without a verse.

steps.title: The זבה verse is needed: זיבה is more lenient than נדה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that we could not learn זיבה from נדה, because נדה is stricter.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed. If the תורה had written it only about נדה, I would have said: נדה applies to a baby because it is strict, since one day of seeing requires her to sit seven days. But a זבה, who after seeing one day only needs to keep one clean day for that day, I would say does not apply. So it is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the verse for a ten-day-old זבה is necessary. Without it, we might have thought only the strict law of נדה applies to a young girl.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נדה who sees even one day must wait seven days, which is strict. A woman who sees one day during the זיבה days only waits one clean day, which is lenient. Since זיבה looks lighter, we might have said it does not apply to a baby, so the verse is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed; this source is necessary and cannot be learned from the other case
She keeps one clean day for each day of seeing (the lighter form of זבה)

phrases.english: It is needed, because if the Merciful One had written it about נדה,
I would have said: נדה applies,
because when she sees blood for one day,
she must sit seven days;

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל זָבָה, דְּאִי חֲזַאי חַד יוֹמָא —
phrases.english: but a זבה, who, if she sees for one day,

phrases.aramaic: בְּשׁוֹמֶרֶת יוֹם כְּנֶגֶד יוֹם סַגִּי לַהּ,
phrases.english: it is enough for her to keep a day for a day,
phrases.notes: She waits one clean day for her one day of seeing, much lighter than seven.

phrases.english: I would say it does not apply. So it is needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the ברייתא against the challenge in step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: shows the lesson cannot be learned from the other case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since נדה is strict and זיבה can be lenient, maybe a baby is only subject to נדה.
steps.terutzMaskana: A verse is needed to include a ten-day-old girl in זיבה.

steps.title: Then write only זבה, and נדה would be known from it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: the תורה could have written only the זבה case, and we would know the נדה case by ourselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the Merciful One write it about a זבה and not need it about נדה, and I would know, because there is no זבה without נדה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא flips the question. If the verse for a ten-day-old זבה is needed, then the separate source for a one-day-old נדה seems extra.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A girl can only become a זבה after first being a נדה. So if a ten-day-old can be a זבה, she must already have been a נדה from day one. The נדה verse now looks unnecessary.

keyTerms.meaning: Let the Merciful One (the תורה) write
There is no זבה without (first being) a נדה

phrases.english: Then let the Merciful One write it about a זבה,
and it would not be needed about נדה,

phrases.aramaic: וַאֲנָא יָדַעְנָא דְּאֵין זָבָה בְּלֹא נִדָּה.
phrases.english: and I would know it, since there is no זבה without נדה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer in step 3 to show the other verse is now extra.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for a separate source that a one-day-old girl is a נדה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Since זבה always comes after נדה, the זבה source already proves the נדה law.

steps.title: Agreed, so the נדה verse excludes a man from red
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that the נדה law is learned from זבה, which frees the נדה verse to teach that a man is not impure through red.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, it is indeed so! Then why do I need the verse? To exclude a man from red.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the challenge. It then explains that the extra verse is not wasted: it teaches that a man is not impure through red, which was the answer in step 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the baby-נדה law comes from the זבה verse, the extra word in the נדה verse is free. That free word is used to exclude a man from red. This confirms the opening answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes, that is indeed so (the גמרא agrees)
Why do I need the verse?

steps.whatToRemember: There is no זבה without נדה, so the source for a ten-day-old זבה also covers a one-day-old נדה. That frees the extra word in the נדה verse to teach that a man is not impure through red.
steps.confusionAlert: "למעוטי איש מאודם" appears twice. The גמרא is not starting over: the second time it confirms that the verse really is free for this teaching.

phrases.english: Yes, it is indeed so!
Then why do I need the verse?
phrases.notes: This is the extra "ואשה" in the נדה verse, ויקרא 15:19.

phrases.english: To exclude a man from red.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts the challenge of step 4 and brings the discussion back to the answer of step 1.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The נדה law for a baby is learned from the זבה verse, and the extra word "ואשה" in the נדה verse teaches that a man is not impure through a red discharge.

steps.title: But the תורה already excluded this once
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a man not becoming impure through red was already excluded by another source, so why exclude it again from the נדה verse?
steps.simpleTranslation: But you already excluded it one time!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the conclusion of Step 5. It says this exclusion was already learned elsewhere.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 5 the extra נדה verse was freed up to teach that a man is not impure through red. But the תורה already excluded that once in an earlier derivation. If so, the second exclusion seems useless.

keyTerms.meaning: You excluded it (from מִיעוּט, a limitation drawn from a פסוק)

phrases.english: But you already excluded it one time?
phrases.notes: He means an earlier derivation that already taught a man is not impure through red.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the conclusion of Step 5 by pointing out a double exclusion.
steps.kashyaTarget: The use of the נדה verse to exclude a man from impurity through red
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A law the תורה already taught once cannot be what a second verse comes to teach, so the second verse would be extra.

steps.title: One exclusion is for semen, one is for blood
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the two exclusions teach two different things: one is about red semen and one is about blood.
steps.simpleTranslation: One verse excludes a man from impurity through red semen, and the other excludes him from impurity through blood.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers Step 6. The two exclusions are not repeats, because each one covers a different kind of red discharge.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Red semen and blood are two different things. So the Torah needs one exclusion for each. Neither verse is extra.

phrases.english: One is to exclude him from impurity through semen,
phrases.notes: This means semen that comes out red.

phrases.english: and one is to exclude him from impurity through blood.

steps.triggerLanguage: חַד לְמַעוֹטֵי מִשִּׁכְבַת זֶרַע, וְחַד לְמַעוֹטֵי מִדָּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two exclusions into two separate cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both verses teach the same exclusion, so one of them is extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: One verse excludes red semen and the other excludes blood, so both are needed.
steps.whatToRemember: A man does not become impure through a red discharge, whether it is red semen or blood. Each has its own source.

steps.title: Even a one-day-old boy can become a זב
steps.stepSummary: Like the ten-day-old girl, a boy can also become a זב. רבי יהודה learns from the double word "איש איש" that even a one-day-old baby boy can become impure with זיבה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The same is true for males. As a ברייתא teaches: Why does the פסוק say "any man" (literally "a man, a man")? To include a one-day-old baby, who can become impure through זיבה. This is the view of רבי יהודה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves from girls to boys. It brings a ברייתא showing that a baby boy, even one day old, can become a זב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, "ואשה" taught that a ten-day-old girl can be a זבה. Here, the double word "איש איש" in the זב section works the same way for boys. For רבי יהודה, the extra "איש" includes even a newborn.

keyTerms.meaning: "The verse teaches," used to ask or show why a פסוק says something
The impurity of a זב, from an abnormal discharge

phrases.english: And so too regarding males.
phrases.notes: Just like the ten-day-old girl from Step 2, a young boy can also become impure.

phrases.english: As it is taught: "Any man" (literally, "a man, a man").
Why does the verse say "a man, a man"?
To include a one-day-old baby,
that he becomes impure through זיבה.
These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels the girl's case from Step 2 with a boy's case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, "איש איש" includes a one-day-old boy in the laws of זיבה.

steps.title: Same law, different source: "לזכר ולנקבה"
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה agrees that babies can become impure with זיבה, but he learns it from "לזכר ולנקבה." He says the double "איש איש" teaches nothing, because the תורה speaks the way people speak.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל בנו של רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה says: That derivation is not needed. The פסוק says "for the male and for the female." "For the male" means any male, adult or child. "For the female" means any female, adult or child. If so, why does it say "a man, a man"? The תורה spoke the way people speak.
steps.whatsHappening: A second תנא agrees with the law but gives it a different source. Because of that, he says the double word "איש איש" has nothing to teach.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both תנאים agree that young children can become impure with זיבה. They only argue about which פסוק teaches it. For רבי ישמעאל, "לזכר ולנקבה" already covers every age, so the doubled "איש" is just normal speech.

keyTerms.meaning: The תורה spoke in the language of people, so a doubled word need not teach anything extra

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the two תנאים argue about the law itself. Both agree a baby can become a זב. They only argue about which פסוק is the source.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yochanan ben Beroka, says:
It is not needed, for it says:
"For the male and for the female."
"For the male" means anyone who is male,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁהוּא גָּדוֹל בֵּין שֶׁהוּא קָטָן,
phrases.english: whether he is an adult or whether he is a minor;
"and for the female" means anyone who is female,
whether an adult or a minor.

phrases.aramaic: אִם כֵּן, מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״אִישׁ אִישׁ״?
phrases.english: If so, why does the verse say "a man, a man"?
The Torah spoke in the language of people.
phrases.notes: People often repeat a word when they talk, so the repeat here is not meant to teach anything.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּנוֹ שֶׁל רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה אוֹמֵר: אֵין צָרִיךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different source for the same law taught in Step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "לזכר ולנקבה" includes males and females of every age in זיבה. "איש איש" is ordinary speech.

steps.title: One day old or nine years old?
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא the גמרא infers that when a פסוק includes a boy, it includes even a one-day-old. It then brings a different ברייתא in which "ואיש" includes a boy only from nine years and one day, which seems to contradict this.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it seems that when a פסוק includes a boy, it includes even a one-day-old. But this contradicts another ברייתא: "Man" teaches only an adult man. From where do we know that a boy of nine years and one day is included? The פסוק says "And a man."
steps.whatsHappening: First the גמרא draws a rule from the ברייתא, which sets up the next move. Then it brings another ברייתא that seems to clash with that rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the זיבה ברייתא, the extra word includes a baby even one day old. In the second ברייתא, about semen, the extra "ו" of "ואיש" includes a boy only from age nine years and one day. Two similar inclusions give two different ages, and the גמרא wants to know why.

keyTerms.meaning: And they contradicted them: a contradiction is raised from another source
A boy aged nine years and one day

phrases.english: Evidently, when the verse includes a boy,
it includes even a one-day-old.
But raise a contradiction from another ברייתא:
"Man": I only know about an adult man.
phrases.notes: This ברייתא is on the פסוק about semen, ויקרא 15:16.

phrases.aramaic: בֶּן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד מִנַּיִן?
phrases.english: From where do we know about a boy of nine years and one day?
The verse says: "And a man."
phrases.notes: The extra letter ו, "and," is what includes the younger boy.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא, כִּי מְרַבֵּי קְרָא בֶּן יוֹם אֶחָד מְרַבֵּי. וּרְמִינְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a rule from Steps 8 and 9 and then challenges it with a different ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that an inclusion of a boy in the פסוק covers even a one-day-old
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A parallel inclusion ("ואיש" about semen) reaches down only to nine years and one day, not to a newborn, so the two ברייתות seem to contradict each other.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next answer, which will have to explain why the age limit differs between the two cases.

steps.title: רבא: These are traditions only hinted at in the verses
steps.stepSummary: רבא resolves the contradiction by saying these rules are הלכות from סיני, and the רבנן only hung them on פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: These are traditions passed down from סיני, and the רבנן just attached them to verses.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the contradiction from step 10. He says the two ברייתות are not really arguing about how to read פסוקים, because these rules come from a tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction depended on both rules being learned from the פסוק. רבא says at least one of them is really a הלכה למשה מסיני, and the פסוק is only a hint (אסמכתא). So the two ways of reading the verses do not have to match.

keyTerms.meaning: A tradition passed down from משה at סיני (הלכה למשה מסיני)
They leaned it on: the רבנן attached the rule to a פסוק as a support

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea: sometimes a פסוק is only a hint for a rule we really know from tradition, so its wording should not be pushed too far.

phrases.english: Rava said:
They are traditional laws (from Sinai),
and the Rabbis leaned them on verses.
phrases.notes: He means the verse is not the real source, just a hook to remember the rule by.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 10.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reclassifying the source: the rule comes from tradition, not from a true reading of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both age rules come from reading the פסוקים, so they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The rules are הלכות from סיני, only supported by פסוקים, so there is no real contradiction.

steps.title: Which rule is the tradition and which is the verse?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which of the two rules is the tradition and which one is truly learned from the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which one is the tradition, and which one is from the verse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about רבא's answer. This sets up the next two steps, which test each possibility.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's answer only works if one rule is tradition and the other comes from the פסוק. Now the גמרא needs to figure out which is which: the one-day-old rule or the nine-years-and-one-day rule.

phrases.english: Which is the tradition, and which is the verse?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for clarification of רבא's answer in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the one-day-old rule or the nine-year rule is the tradition from סיני.

steps.title: The one-day-old rule cannot be the tradition
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tests the first option, that the one-day-old rule is tradition and the nine-year rule is from the פסוק, and rejects it because the פסוק is written without any age.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say the one-day-old rule is the tradition and the nine-years-and-one-day rule is from the verse, that cannot be: the verse is written with no age limit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries the first possibility and pushes it away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse "ואיש" gives no age. If we really learned from it, it would include every boy, even a one-day-old. So the verse itself cannot be the source for a minimum age of nine years and one day.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion that will be tested)
A boy aged nine years and one day

phrases.english: If you say the one-day-old is from tradition,

phrases.aramaic: וּבֶן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד — קְרָא,
phrases.english: and the boy of nine years and one day is from the verse,
but the verse is written with no limit!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests and rejects the first answer to step 12's question.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggestion that the nine-year rule comes from the פסוק
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A verse with no stated age cannot produce a minimum age.

steps.title: The nine-year rule is the tradition and the baby rule is from the verse
steps.stepSummary: Instead, the nine-years-and-one-day rule is the tradition, and the one-day-old rule comes from the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the nine-years-and-one-day rule is the tradition, and the one-day-old rule is from the verse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct way to divide the two rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a verse with no age fits a one-day-old, the baby rule is the one truly learned from the פסוק. The minimum age of nine years and one day comes from a tradition from סיני, not from reading the verse.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא בֶּן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד — הִלְכְתָא,
phrases.english: Rather, the boy of nine years and one day is from tradition,
and the one-day-old is from the verse.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא בֶּן תֵּשַׁע שָׁנִים וְיוֹם אֶחָד — הִלְכְתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the accepted answer after step 13 rejected the first option.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The nine-year rule is a tradition from סיני, and the one-day-old rule is learned from the פסוק.

steps.title: If it is a tradition, why do we need the verse?
steps.stepSummary: If the nine-year rule is a tradition, the גמרא asks what the verse "ואיש" is needed for.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since it is a tradition, why do I need the verse?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. If the nine-year rule comes from tradition, the extra word in the פסוק seems to have no job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק is not supposed to have extra words that teach nothing. Since the rule is already known from tradition, the גמרא wants to know what the word "ואיש" actually teaches.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (asking what a word or source is for)

phrases.english: And now that it is a tradition,
why do I need the verse?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דְּהִלְכְתָא הִיא, קְרָא לְמָה לִי?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the result of step 14.
steps.kashyaTarget: The verse "ואיש" in the ברייתא about the nine-year-old
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rule is known from tradition, the verse seems to be extra.

steps.title: The verse excludes a woman from a white discharge
steps.stepSummary: The verse is needed to teach that a woman does not become impure through a white discharge.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse comes to exclude a woman from becoming impure through a white discharge.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the verse has a different job of its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse is not needed for the age rule, which comes from tradition. Instead, it teaches that a woman does not become a זבה from a white discharge. That kind of impurity belongs to a man.

phrases.english: To exclude a woman from a white discharge.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Giving the verse a different purpose
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The verse is extra, because the age rule is already known from tradition.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse teaches that a woman is not made impure by a white discharge.
steps.whatToRemember: The nine-years-and-one-day rule is a tradition from סיני. The one-day-old rule comes from a פסוק. The extra word in the ברייתא's verse teaches that a woman is not made impure by a white discharge.

steps.title: Why teach the baby rule for both males and females?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the תורה needs to teach the rule that babies can become impure for both boys and girls.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need it written for males, and why do I need it written for females?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question: why the תורה repeats the baby rule for both boys and girls. This sets up a צריכותא, an explanation of why both are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the גמרא learned from פסוקים that a baby boy can become a זב and that a little girl can become a נדה or a זבה. If one case could be learned from the other, writing both would be extra.

phrases.english: Why do I need it written about males,
and why do I need it written about females?
phrases.notes: This is about the earlier lessons that even babies can become impure, for boys and for girls.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמָה לִי לְמִכְתַּב בִּזְכָרִים, וּלְמָה לִי לְמִכְתַּב בִּנְקֵבוֹת?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the baby-impurity rules from steps 8 and 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the תורה writes the baby rule for both boys and girls, instead of learning one from the other.

steps.title: Both are needed: men are stricter because of sightings in one day
steps.stepSummary: Both are needed. If the תורה had written only about males, we would think the rule applies only to them, because males are stricter: three sightings in one day count like three sightings on three days.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both are necessary. If the תורה had written it only about males, we would say it applies to them because they become impure through sightings in one day just like sightings over days. But females, who do not become impure that way, we would say are not included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer, called a צריכותא. It explains why writing the rule only for males would not teach us about females.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A זב becomes impure from three sightings even on a single day, just as from sightings on three days. A זבה needs three separate days. Since males are stricter, we might have thought only males are included even as babies.

keyTerms.meaning: Both are necessary (opens a צריכותא, showing why each source is needed)
The Merciful One: a name for ה׳ as the giver of the Torah
Sightings: times a discharge is seen
Like days: counted the same as sightings on separate days

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up "ראיות" (sightings) with "ראיה" (proof). Here it means times a discharge is seen.

phrases.english: They are necessary,
because if the Merciful One had written it about males,
that would be because they become impure through sightings as through days,
phrases.notes: For a man, three sightings on one day count the same as sightings on three separate days.

phrases.english: but females,
who do not become impure through sightings as through days,
I would say not.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the question of step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: showing that each source teaches something the other could not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From males alone, we would think females are not included, because males are stricter.
steps.terutzMaskana: So the תורה had to write the rule for females too.

steps.title: Why the girls' verse alone would not be enough
steps.stepSummary: If the תורה had written only about girls, we might think boys are left out, because a girl becomes impure even from a discharge caused by an outside factor, and a boy does not. So both verses are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the תורה had written only about females, I would say the rule applies to them because they become impure even from something beyond their control. But males, who do not become impure from something beyond their control, I would say are not included. So both verses are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from the last step by showing the other side: writing only about girls would also not have been enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 18 showed that writing only about boys would leave out girls, because boys are stricter in one way. Here the גמרא shows that girls are stricter in a different way: they become impure even through אונס. Since each one is stricter in its own way, we could not learn one from the other, so the תורה had to write both.

keyTerms.meaning: Something beyond one's control; here, a discharge caused by an outside factor
It is needed; both sources are necessary

steps.whatToRemember: Boys and girls are each stricter in a different way, so the תורה had to teach baby impurity for both.

phrases.english: And if the Merciful One had written only about females,
[I would say it applies to them] because they become impure even through something beyond their control,
but males, who do not become impure through something beyond their control,
I would say not. So both are needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the second half of the צריכותא begun in step 18
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each case has its own stringency, so neither can be learned from the other
steps.terutzHavaAmina: With only the females' verse, we would exclude males because they are not made impure by אונס

steps.title: The משנה's rule about כותים and bedding
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a new line of the משנה: כותים make the lower bedding impure like the upper bedding.
steps.simpleTranslation: The כותים make the lower bedding impure like the upper bedding.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording 'lower like upper' is unclear. It could mean that a whole stack of bedding becomes impure, or it could be comparing two kinds of impurity. The next steps work out which meaning is right.

keyTerms.meaning: Bedding, something one lies or sits on

phrases.english: The כותים make impure
the lower bedding like the upper.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New topic; quotes the next clause of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כותים impart impurity to lower bedding like upper bedding

steps.title: What does 'lower like upper' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה means by 'lower bedding like upper bedding.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'lower bedding like upper bedding' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the meaning of the unclear phrase in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real question about wording, not an attack. The גמרא wants to know exactly what is being compared to what.

phrases.english: What does 'lower bedding like upper' mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the משנה just quoted
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of 'lower bedding like upper'

steps.title: The stack-of-mattresses reading is too obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests it means a כותי sitting on ten stacked mattresses makes all of them impure, then rejects this because it is obvious: he presses on all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means that when there are ten mattresses and he sits on them he makes them all impure, that is obvious, because he presses on all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a simple reading of the משנה and throws it out because the משנה would not need to teach something so obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bedding becomes impure through pressure from the impure person sitting on it. Even the bottom mattress feels that pressure, so of course it is impure like the top ones. The משנה must be teaching something new.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say; introduces a reading that will be rejected

phrases.english: If you say it means that if there are ten mattresses
and he sits on them, he makes them impure,
phrases.notes: The word in round brackets is in the printed גמרא; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: that is obvious! Because he presses on them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first answer to the question and rejects it
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects reading 'lower like upper' as a stack of mattresses
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That reading teaches nothing new, since pressure reaches all layers

steps.title: Bedding under a בועל נדה is like bedding above a זב
steps.stepSummary: The משנה means that bedding under a man who had relations with a נדה has the same weaker impurity as bedding above a זב: it makes only food and drink impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means that what is under a man who had relations with a נדה is like what is above a זב. Just as what is above a זב makes only food and drink impure, so too what is under a man who had relations with a נדה makes only food and drink impure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the correct meaning: the משנה is comparing two levels of impurity, not two layers of mattresses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bedding under a זב becomes a strong source of impurity. Bedding under a בועל נדה is weaker: like bedding above a זב, it only makes food and drink impure, not people or utensils. So 'lower like upper' means 'the lower of a בועל נדה is like the upper of a זב.'

keyTerms.meaning: A man who had relations with a woman who is a נדה
A man with a certain kind of discharge that makes him impure

steps.confusionAlert: 'Lower' and 'upper' here are not two mattresses of the same person. 'Lower' is bedding under a בועל נדה, and 'upper' is bedding above a זב.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the bedding of a בועל נדה is a weaker level of impurity than the bedding of a זב.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, שֶׁיְּהֵא תַּחְתּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל בּוֹעֵל נִדָּה
phrases.english: Rather, it means that what is under a man who had relations with a נדה
phrases.notes: The גמרא assumes the כותים count as men who had relations with a נדה. That is why their bedding comes up here.

phrases.english: is like what is above a זב.
Just as what is above a זב
makes only food and drink impure,
so too what is under a man who had relations with a נדה
makes only food and drink impure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא שֶׁיְּהֵא תַּחְתּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל בּוֹעֵל נִדָּה כְּעֶלְיוֹנוֹ שֶׁל זָב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading with the correct one
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Lower bedding of a בועל נדה equals upper bedding of a זב: it imparts impurity only to food and drink

steps.title: Where do we learn the rule about bedding above a זב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that bedding above a זב makes only food and drink impure.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is above a זב — where do we learn this from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks for the תורה source of the rule it just used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The explanation in the last step depends on the rule about bedding above a זב. Before relying on it, the גמרא wants to know where that rule comes from.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know this?

phrases.english: What is above a זב — from where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the rule used in step 23
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that bedding above a זב imparts impurity only to food and drink

steps.title: The source begins with the פסוק about 'under him'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק 'whoever touches anything that will be under him shall be impure' and asks what 'under him' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And whoever touches anything that will be under him shall be impure.' What does 'under him' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins its answer by quoting a פסוק, then asks how to read the words 'under him.' The full explanation continues in the next part of the גמרא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source for bedding above a זב is a פסוק that says 'under him.' That seems surprising, so the גמרא stops to ask what 'under him' really means. The answer comes next.

phrases.english: As it is written: 'And whoever touches
anything that will be under him shall be impure.'
What does 'under him' mean?

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב וְכׇל הַנּוֹגֵעַ בְּכֹל אֲשֶׁר יִהְיֶה תַחְתָּיו יִטְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the source question with a פסוק and a question about its wording
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is ויקרא 15:10; the reading of 'under him' is about to be explained
